test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: From the top of a 60 m high building, the angles of depression of the top and bottom of a lamp post are 30° and 60°, respectively. Find the height of the lamp post.
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Height of building (H) = 60 m.

Ratio of heights H : (H − h) = tan 60° : tan 30° = √3 : (1/√3) = 3 : 1.

Total height 3 units → 60 m, so 1 unit → 20 m.

Lamp post height (h) = 3 units − 1 unit = 2 units → 2 × 20 = 40 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 40 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b6e55d7d6407a0150e8cf99a283373f64da8582410e0bd5374331d3e4a4d625f.png] 

**Given:** Height of building AB = 60 m. Let height of lamp post CD = h. Distance BD = x.

**Formula Used:** tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

⇒ In ΔABD: tan 60° = AB / BD

⇒ √3 = 60 / x

⇒ x = 60 / √3 = 20√3 m

⇒ In small triangle at top (height 60 − h): tan 30° = (60 − h) / x

⇒ 1 / √3 = (60 − h) / (20√3)

⇒ 20√3 / √3 = 60 − h

⇒ 20 = 60 − h

⇒ h = 60 − 20 = 40 m

**∴ The correct answer is 40 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Angle of Depression

The angle formed between the **horizontal line** and the line of sight when looking **downwards** at an object.

Standard Ratios for 30-60-90 Triangles

In a right triangle with angles 30° and 60°, the sides opposite to them are in the ratio **1 : √3 : 2** respectively.

Relationship between two heights

When the distance is same, h = H × (1 − tan θ₁ / tan θ₂) where θ₁ is the top angle and θ₂ is the bottom angle.</p
